h1: Prop firms that allow bots and EAs
title: Prop Firms That Allow Bots and EAs ({month})
description: Prop firms that permit expert advisors and automated trading, and the limits each one sets on bots, HFT and copy trading.
intro: Many futures firms ban or tightly restrict automation. These firms allow it, each with its own limits: high-frequency trading and copying the same bot across users are banned almost everywhere. Read the firm's rules on your own bot before you buy.

h1: Prop firms with no consistency rule
title: Prop Firms With No Consistency Rule ({month})
description: Prop firms with no consistency rule in the evaluation, which also have none on funded payouts, and the payout caps each one sets.
blurb: No best-day cap in the evaluation
intro: Every firm below has at least one plan with no consistency rule in the evaluation, so one big day cannot fail you or raise your target. If you also want no consistency rule on funded payouts, the forex firms are the easier pick: FTMO's 2-Step, Goat Funded Trader, Maven, BrightFunded, Blueberry Funded's Prime and 1-Step, FunderPro's Classic and Funding Traders' 2-Step Pro10 have none at either stage. Most futures firms add one once you are funded, before a payout; the table shows where.
body:
No consistency rule and no payout cap?

Futures firms almost always cap how much you can take out per payout, even when they have no consistency rule. These are the 50K caps their own payout pages state:

Tradeify Growth35% on every payout request$1,500, rising to $3,000 from payout 4

For the forex firms named at the top, we did not find a fixed dollar cap per payout in the rules we checked. Their limits work differently: a minimum profit before a request, a fixed payout cycle (every 10 to 21 days) or a minimum number of profitable days. Confirm on the firm's own payout page before you rely on it, and see how prop firm payouts work.
faq: Which prop firm does not have a consistency rule?

Among the firms we track, FTMO's 2-Step, Goat Funded Trader, Maven, BrightFunded, Blueberry Funded (Prime and 1-Step), FunderPro Classic and Funding Traders' 2-Step Pro10 have no consistency rule in the evaluation or on funded payouts. Apex, Tradeify Growth, MyFundedFutures, Phidias and Bulenox have none in the evaluation, but most of them add one before funded payouts.
Which prop firm has no consistency rule and no payout cap?

Futures firms usually cap each payout: for example $2,000 at Topstep (XFA Standard) and Lucid, and $1,500 to $3,000 at Apex and Tradeify Growth on 50K. Forex firms with no consistency rule, such as FTMO's 2-Step, Goat Funded Trader and BrightFunded, use payout cycles and minimums instead; we did not find a fixed per-payout dollar cap in their rules, but check the firm's payout page.
What is a consistency rule?

A limit on how much of your total profit can come from your best day, for example 40% or 50%. Break it in the evaluation and you either fail or have to keep trading until your other days catch up; break it on a funded account and the payout is usually delayed. See our consistency rule guide.

title: Prop Firms With End-of-Day Drawdown ({month})
description: Futures prop firms whose max loss trails only at the daily close, so open profit you give back intraday does not tighten your limit.
blurb: Max loss moves only at the close
intro: With end-of-day trailing drawdown, your loss limit moves only at the daily close, so profit you give back during the day does not tighten it. Firms marked "depends on plan" also sell an intraday version. See how trailing drawdown works.
faq: Which futures prop firms offer end-of-day trailing drawdown?

Among the firms we track: Topstep, Tradeify, Lucid, Alpha Futures, Funded Futures Network, MyFundedFutures (Builder, Rapid EOD and Pro), Phidias (Fundamental and Premium), Top One Futures, Hola Prime futures and Bulenox (end-of-day option). Apex and TradeDay let you choose end-of-day or intraday.
Which futures prop firms have intraday trailing drawdown?

Apex sells an intraday trailing evaluation and performance account alongside its end-of-day one, and TradeDay lets you choose intraday in the evaluation. Take Profit Trader uses end-of-day in the Test but intraday on PRO accounts, MyFundedFutures' Rapid plan switches to intraday once funded, and Earn2Trade uses intraday trailing on Live accounts.
Which prop firm has the lowest drawdown?

The smallest 50K max loss we track is Phidias' Express to Live account: $650, static. Maven's Standard 3 Step allows 3% ($1,500), also static. A smaller drawdown is cheaper or faster to pass but leaves very little room; see the biggest-drawdown list for the other end.
body: Looking for the most room instead? See prop firms with the biggest drawdown. To see how end-of-day and intraday trailing behave on the same trades, try the drawdown simulator.

title: Instant Funding Prop Firms ({month}): Skip the Evaluation
description: Prop firms that sell a funded account with no evaluation, what they cost and the stricter rules that usually come with them.
blurb: Funded account without an evaluation, and the catch
intro: Yes, these firms sell a funded account with no evaluation phase: you pay more up front and trade for payouts from day one. The catch is stricter rules, usually a consistency requirement, a profit buffer you must build before the first payout, or lower payout caps. These firms sell an instant or direct account alongside their evaluations; open each review for the instant plan's terms.
faq: Which instant funding prop firms skip the evaluation phase?

All firms on this page sell at least one account with no evaluation, including Tradeify (Lightning Funded), Alpha Futures (Direct), Funding Traders, Aqua Funded, Alpha Capital Group (Alpha Direct) and FTMO. The account is funded from the start, but you still have to meet payout conditions.
What is the catch with instant funding?

Stricter payout rules. For example, Tradeify's Lightning Funded applies a 20% consistency rule to the first payout and has a $1,000 minimum payout on 50K; Funding Traders' Instant account needs the balance 3.5% above the starting size and a 15% consistency score; Alpha Capital's Alpha Direct needs a 3% profit buffer and a 15% best-day rule; Aqua Funded's Instant Pro uses a 20% consistency rule.
Is instant funding worth it?

It costs more than an evaluation for the same account size, and the payout rules are tighter. It suits traders who are confident in their consistency and want to skip paying for a test first. Compare the total cost with the challenge cost calculator.

title: Prop Firms for US Traders: Which Accept US Residents ({month})
description: Which futures and forex prop firms accept US residents, which platforms US traders can use at each, and which firms do not serve the US. Checked against each firm's own pages.
blurb: US residents accepted, per each firm's own pages
intro: Every firm below says on its own pages that it accepts US residents, or leaves the US off its restricted-country list. Futures firms are the simplest option for US traders. Forex firms often do accept US residents, but usually not on MetaTrader 5, so check the platform before you buy.
body:
Futures or forex?

Futures prop firms such as Topstep, Apex, Tradeify, Lucid, MyFundedFutures, Alpha Futures, Phidias, TradeDay, Funded Futures Network and Earn2Trade all accept US residents. Their evaluations run on US futures platforms like Tradovate, NinjaTrader and Rithmic, so there is no platform catch.

Forex and CFD firms are different. Several of them say MetaTrader 5 is not available to US residents, so US traders get a smaller set of platforms:

  • FTMO: US clients are served through a separate US offering at ftmo.oanda.com.
  • E8 Markets: no MT5 for US citizens; US traders use TradeLocker, cTrader or Match-Trader through E8's US entity.
  • Goat Funded Trader: no MT5 or cTrader for US clients; TradeLocker, Match-Trader and Volumetrica are available.
  • Hola Prime: US clients can trade forex on Match-Trader and TradeLocker only.

Firms where US access is limited or unclear

These firms do not list the US as restricted, but limit what US residents can use, or do not say clearly: FunderPro (TradeLocker challenges only), Maven Trading (Match Trader only), BrightFunded (DXtrade only), The5ers (no MT5 for US residents) Funding Traders (MT5 not intended for US residents) and Alpha Capital Group (its help center says US residents can use DXtrade and TradeLocker, but its order form asks you to confirm you are not a US resident). For Aqua Funded, FundingPips, Blue Guardian, Bulenox, Take Profit Trader and Top One Futures, we could not find a clear statement either way. Ask the firm before you pay.

Firms that do not accept US residents

FXIFY and Blueberry Funded list the United States as a restricted country.
faq: Can US residents use prop firms?
Yes. Most futures prop firms accept US residents, including Topstep, Apex, Tradeify, Lucid and MyFundedFutures. Many forex prop firms accept them too, but often not on MetaTrader 5.
Why can't US traders use MT5 at some prop firms?

Several forex prop firms, including E8, Goat Funded Trader, FunderPro and The5ers, say MetaTrader 5 is not available to US residents. They offer other platforms such as TradeLocker, Match-Trader, cTrader or DXtrade instead. The firms do not all give a reason.
Which prop firms do not accept US traders?
Among the firms we track, FXIFY and Blueberry Funded list the United States as restricted.
Is FTMO available in the US?
Yes, through a separate US offering run with OANDA at ftmo.oanda.com.
Can I trade gold and crypto with a funded account from the US?

Yes, most simply through futures prop firms: Topstep, MyFundedFutures and Phidias list COMEX metals (gold futures) and CME crypto micros such as Micro Bitcoin and Micro Ether among their instruments, and Alpha Futures lists Micro Bitcoin and Micro Ether. On the forex side, FTMO's US version lists gold, silver and BTCUSD.
Which prop firm has the best payouts for US traders?

It depends on what you value. Apex pays 100% of approved payouts on its performance accounts; Topstep, Tradeify, Lucid and Alpha Futures pay 90%. MyFundedFutures pays every 48 hours on Builder and daily on Rapid, but most firms also cap each payout, for example $2,000 at Topstep (XFA Standard) and Lucid on 50K. See how prop firm payouts work for the full rules.

h1: Prop firms with the biggest drawdown
title: Prop Firms With the Biggest Drawdown on a 50K Account ({month})
description: Which prop firms give the largest max loss (drawdown) on a 50K account, ranked by dollar amount, with the plan and drawdown type for each.
blurb: Ranked by the largest 50K max loss
intro: These firms are ranked by the largest maximum loss they allow on a 50K account, across all of their plans. A bigger drawdown gives you more room before the account fails, but the type matters as much as the size: a static limit stays put, while a trailing limit follows your profits up.
body:
Bigger is not always looser

Compare drawdowns of the same type. A $5,000 static max loss never moves, so every dollar of profit widens your cushion. A $2,000 end-of-day trailing drawdown rises with your best closing balance, so the cushion can shrink after a good day. Intraday trailing is the tightest, because it also follows open profit. See trailing drawdown explained, or try the drawdown simulator with your own days.

Check the daily loss limit too

Most forex firms with a large max loss also have a daily loss limit, often 4% or 5% of the account. On a 50K account that is $2,000 to $2,500 in one day, whatever the overall drawdown. Each review lists both.

Futures vs forex

Forex and CFD firms usually set the max loss as a percentage of the account, often 8% to 12%. Futures firms usually set a fixed dollar amount instead, typically $2,000 (sometimes $2,500) on a 50K account, usually trailing.
faq: Which prop firm has the biggest drawdown?
Among the firms we track, the largest 50K max loss is at the top of the list on this page, with the plan it applies to. Rankings change when firms change their rules, so check the date at the top.
Is a static or trailing drawdown better?

For the same dollar amount, static is easier: the limit never moves, so profits add to your cushion. A trailing drawdown follows your highest balance up, which can leave you with less room after a good run.
